# FDG7058

> DO make exceptions runtime serializable. An exception must be serializable to work correctly across application domain and remoting boundaries.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.4 Designing Custom Exceptions.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA2237
- Automatic fix: yes
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

CA2237 reports a type that itself lists ISerializable, as in the example of FDG7059, without SerializableAttribute, and only when the target is .NET Framework, where application domain and remoting boundaries exist (probe with SDK 10.0.402: net472 reported, net10.0 did not). Exceptions that inherit ISerializable only from System.Exception are not reported, so coverage is partial. Its code fix adds the attribute, which changes no signature. Analyzer candidate rejected: the reason of the text does not exist on .NET Core, BinaryFormatter was removed in .NET 9, and .NET 8 made the serialization constructor and GetObjectData of exceptions obsolete (SYSLIB0051), so a check on every exception type would ask for serialization support that current .NET no longer uses.
